newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Pick says HI figures show higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Pick says HI figures show higher profits.

text.p: First-half figures not yet released by meat processor Pick Szeged Rt promise higher sales and profits, the company's CEO told Reuters.
"Our first half figures fulfil our plans," Vilmos Bihari said.
Asked whether this meant increased profits, Bihari said the company would have better profits margins than in the first half of 1996.
The company registered a consolidated pretax profit of 901.5 nillion forints on sales of 12.447 billion forints in the first half of 1996.
Pick plans to increase its sales by 25 percent in 1997, mainly by increasing exports.

Its principle foreign market is Germany, which accounts for 78 percent of total export volume, but the company plans large growth for Eastern Europe and targets new markets in France and the Commonwealth of Independent States.
In the first quarter of this year, Pick reported an over 40 percent rise in its consolidated pre-tax profit to 577.6 million forints from 411.1 million.
Bihari said the company would publish its consolidated first half figures in the second week of August.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Pick finished steady on Wednesday at 14,500.
